_note: THE REVEAL, AND IT IS GEOMETRY RATHER THAN A CUTSCENE. The road from the west runs thirty tiles along the gate shelf with granite on both sides and nothing visible past it, and then the shelf ends. This fires on the two tiles where the far wall of the gorge comes into a fifteen-tile screen and the near one stops. No camera move, no fade, nobody talking: the player is already looking at it.

lines: The shelf runs out. There is no wall at the end of it and no railing worth the name.
There is the other half of Skyreach, four hundred feet away across the gorge, lit and working.
Between here and it there is one bridge, and everything else is air.
Two planks wide, fifteen lengths long, and it moves about a finger's width under your boot.
The board at the head of it said to look at the far end. The far end is a very long way off.
Behind you somebody on the landing has stopped what they were doing to watch, which is worse.
One plank. Two cables. Five tiles of gorge, and it is the shortest crossing in the city.
The crews do this eleven times a shift and nobody has ever painted a sign at either end.
Two tiles of air, and then a deck somebody sanded and oiled, and a lamp burning on it.
There is no bridge. There has been no bridge since 1889 and there is not going to be one.
Somebody buys the oil out of the town books every year, and no name is written against it.
